realism.how: A militia or police station of 1989 ran its radio through a desk-top base station: a Czechoslovak, Soviet or East German VHF transceiver set in a low metal and plastic desk cabinet with channel buttons, a speaker, a handset on a cradle and a desk microphone. A duty officer sat at it with a logbook.
realism.current: A beige-grey desk set with buttons, lamps and a coiled handset is what a local dispatcher used every shift; a switchboard with patch cables or a glass-fronted tube radio would be a generation older.
